approach:
Root cause: `refusing_check` (crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-551) is an ordered list of `step!` checks. None compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria, and no rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it. A reading that moves part (3) to `out_of_scope` is therefore accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k; failed attempt 20261030-060839-1njk). The fix is `check_request_parts` as the last step, so every existing refusal keeps its check name. The plan is the previous one (shared `request_own_lines` filter in terms.rs:189; Enumerated and Bullet parts; distinctive-stem coverage; clause-scoped criterion negation; enforcement by code only) with the six findings answered. (F1) A retry request ('try again on <job>') carries no parts, so the parts come from the retried job's request, `attempt.request`: refusing_check shadows `request` just before the last step with the retried request followed by the current one, and the step line stays `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));`. (F2) Criterion text is cleaned before stemming: tokens with '/', '_' or '::' and `cargo`/`git` command spans are dropped, and crate-level path words (crates, src, core, lib, mod, bin and the file extensions) are never stems, so `cargo test -p athena-core` covers nothing. Pooled path stems are the only path contribution. (F3) Alternatives need a real introducer: 'either ... or' spanning the markers, 'one of the following/these/options', 'one of:', 'pick one', 'choose one', 'choose between', 'either of', ' or ' right before the last marker, or a part line ending ' or'. A bare 'pick', 'choose' or 'one of' groups nothing. (F4) On the request side the negator guard applies to the clause that holds the deferral phrase, and the list is criterion 4's words with close variants only (later in restricted forms, out of scope, for now, defer/deferred, follow-up). Skip, skipped, omitted and excluded are removed from the request side; they stay on the criterion side. (F5) A step runs and reads the producer-loop replay send-back (run/mod.rs:2294-2319) and fixes false refusals in the matcher, never in the declared share. (F6) Path stems drop COMMON_WORDS and filler, so the path stems of crates/athena-core/tests/foo.rs are {foo}.

Corrected design points added since the last round (an accepted design stays): the retried job's own request is read for parts; followed-up and merely cited jobs are not, because they built on finished work. The retry text's own sentences also count for request-side deferral.

decisions.choice: 1. Build `request_parts` on a shared line filter. Factor the loop of `plain_request_prose` (terms.rs:189-208: ROOT_CAUSE_ANCHOR and APPROVAL_ANCHOR flags, stop at '## Source' for approved work, drop fenced lines, drop `is_generated_line` lines, terms.rs:62) into `pub(super) fn request_own_lines(request: &str) -> Vec<&str>`. `plain_request_prose` becomes `request_own_lines(request).into_iter().map(plain_line).join("\n")` with identical output. `request_parts` (topics.rs) reads only `request_own_lines`; for an approved-work request it skips the first line (the proposal title). RequestPart = {marker: Option<String>, kind: Enumerated|Bullet, text, group: Option<usize>, optional: bool}. `request_text_acceptance` and `is_bullet` stay unchanged. terms.rs is a listed deliverable.
decisions.reason: Generated and copied text (approved-work '## Source' copies from work_decisions.rs, root-cause title and 'Cause:' lines from hestia.rs, fenced 'Request:' blocks) holds 'Acceptance:' bullets and numbered lists that must never become parts. One filter means a later change to the generated shapes is made once. `request_text_acceptance` is the parse `athena plan` uses (topics.rs plan_entry; steward.rs:587) and the corpus pins its bullet counts, so it stays.

rejected.option: Keep a private skip list in `request_parts`
rejected.why: Misses fences and the approved-work '## Source' copy and drifts from terms.rs.

rejected.option: Extend `is_bullet` to read `N)` and `(a)`
rejected.why: Moves plan acceptance of every queued request and the pinned bullet counts.

rejected.option: Read inline sequences from the whole request
rejected.why: Quoted or copied text with markers would become required parts.

decisions.choice: 2. Place `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));` last in `refusing_check`, after `check_reading_references` (checks.rs:549). It returns Ok when `capability` is none or `question` is some, as `check_governance_coverage` does. Directly before that line add `let request = &request_with_retried_parts(request, attempt);` (a new fn in topics.rs). It returns the request unchanged when `attempt` is None; otherwise `attempt.request`, a blank line, then `request`. The shadow comes after every earlier step, so no other check sees the combined text. Only the retried job (`attempt`) is added. Jobs in `referenced`, even followed-up ones, are not, and a retry of a retry is not chained.
decisions.reason: Finding 1: `read_for` passes `&request.text` (reading.rs:720-726) and a retry's text is 'try again on <job>', so its parts are in `attempt.request` (`EarlierAttempt.request`, reader.rs:40; corpus `earlier()`, refusal_corpus.rs:268). Without this a retry that drops part (3) is accepted, the very case of a job retried after deferring a part. Placing the step last keeps each existing Refuse case's check name; `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on the `check_reading_references` step line and still works. The retried request goes first so the Acceptance section of its text ends at the first unindented non-list line of the retry text, and the retry text's sentences count for request-side deferral (decision 8). Followed-up jobs are not read, since a follow-up builds on finished work and would be refused for parts already landed. Limits (doc comment, CHANGELOG, Risks): a retry that narrows scope in words outside the deferral list is refused until a criterion covers the part; a retried request that is itself a retry has no parts; a retried approved-work request stops at '## Source' and the retry text after it is not read for deferral.

rejected.option: Parse only `request`
rejected.why: Finding 1: retries are never checked.

rejected.option: Change the signature to `check_request_parts(reading, request, attempt)`
rejected.why: Criterion 1 fixes the step line as `step!(check_request_parts(reading, request));`.

rejected.option: Also read `referenced` jobs that are followed up
rejected.why: Their parts were done by the finished job; it would falsely refuse follow-ups.

rejected.option: Place the step early, after `check_criteria_evidence`
rejected.why: It would pre-empt `check_outcome_state` in the delivery cases with `2)` and `(a)` parts.

decisions.choice: 3. Parser kinds. `request_parts` runs over `request_own_lines` with states before / in section / after. Before the heading, Enumerated parts are line-start `N.`, `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` and inline `(1)..(2)..` or `(a)..(b)..` sequences (start at 1 or a, consecutive, 2+ markers, each marker followed by text with a significant stem; the last part ends at the first '. ' or line end). The Acceptance section opens on a trimmed, case-insensitive line equal to `Acceptance:`, `Acceptance criteria:`, `## Acceptance` or `## Acceptance criteria`. Other headings are a stated limit. In the section, a line starting `-`, `*` or `N.` is a Bullet with marker None (no inline scan); `N)`, `(N)`, `a)`, `(a)` lines are Enumerated. Blank and indented lines stay in the section. The section ENDS at the first non-blank line with no leading whitespace that is not a list line. Marker-cited coverage and every marker-based deferral or negation apply only to Enumerated parts.
decisions.reason: Bullets have no marker, so criterion 2's own words 'leaves (3) out ... as a follow-up' do not number bullets by position. StewardRequest puts a `Files:` line after its bullets (steward.rs:581-585), and a later Notes list or copied block must not become required bullets. Many tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests and no heading; a free-form dash bullet is not a named part.

rejected.option: Only the exact line `Acceptance:` opens the section
rejected.why: Hand-written variants leave their bullets unenforced.

rejected.option: Number bullets by position so a marker can cite them
rejected.why: The own-reading case would depend on an unstated choice and criterion 2's '(3) ... follow-up' would cancel itself.

rejected.option: The section never ends, or Enumerated parsing resumes after it
rejected.why: A later Notes or Files list would become required parts.

rejected.option: Treat every dash or star bullet as a part
rejected.why: False refusals over fixtures with free-form bullets.

decisions.choice: 4. Alternatives and optional parts, with real introducers only (finding 3). An inline Enumerated sequence is one group when (i) the text before its first marker in the same sentence holds one of ALT_INTRODUCERS = 'one of the following', 'one of these', 'one of the options', 'one of:', 'pick one', 'choose one', 'choose between', 'pick between', 'either of'; or (ii) it holds 'either' and an ' or ' lies before the last marker ('either as (a) .. or (b) ..'); or (iii) the last marker is directly preceded by 'or' or ', or'. Contiguous line-start parts after a non-part line that holds an ALT_INTRODUCER are one group, and a part line ending ' or' groups with the next part. A bare 'pick', 'choose', 'one of' or 'either' with no 'or' groups nothing. A group is covered when any member is covered, skipped when every member is skipped, and the error names it ('one of (a) ..., (b) ...'). A part is optional, and skipped, when its text after the marker starts with 'optionally' or holds 'if time permits' or 'nice to have'. Groups apply to Enumerated parts only. Known limits (doc comment): an 'or' inside one part's text is not a group; 'either' without markers is not read.
decisions.reason: 'Store it either as (a) a JSON file or (b) a TOML table.' must accept a reading that picks (a). A common lead-in must not turn required parts into a group that one part covers, so 'Pick up where job X left off: (1) .. (2) .. (3) ..' and 'This is one of three fixes: (1) ..' stay required parts. `out_of_scope` never covers, so without groups the only repair would be a criterion for work not being done.

rejected.option: Group on any 'pick', 'choose' or 'one of' before the first marker
rejected.why: Finding 3: ordinary lead-ins would let a reading drop two of three parts, silently.

rejected.option: Treat every (a)/(b) sequence as required parts
rejected.why: Refuses a reading that chose one option, with no honest repair.

rejected.option: Let any reading omit parts that contain 'or'
rejected.why: 'Add a flag or alias' style parts would never be enforced.

decisions.choice: 5. Stems (`part_stems`). Strip a leading `[tag]`. Criterion text only (`criterion_words`, finding 2) is cleaned first: drop tokens holding '/', '_' or '::', drop backtick spans that start with `cargo` or `git`, and drop an unquoted span from the token `cargo` or `git` to the next of '.', ';', ',', ')' or the end. Flags such as --json stay. Then lowercase ASCII alphanumeric words; drop all-digit words and words under 3 letters. For each word w, s = w minus one trailing 's' when w is longer than 3. Drop the word when w or s is in FUNCTION_WORDS (the, and, for, not, with, without, unless, are, its, can, all, any, one, add, use, new, via, per, but, has, how, out, was, may, our, you, see, two, who, why, too, now), COMMON_WORDS (topics.rs:157-161), PART_FILLER (pass, passes, passed, passing, cargo, clippy, fmt, content, behavior) or PATH_CRATE_WORDS (crates, src, core, lib, mod, bin, rs, md, toml, json_ext is NOT listed: only the extensions rs, md, toml, yml, yaml, lock, txt). Keep s cut to 6 chars; map `doc` to `docume`. `stems_match(a,b)`: equal, or the shorter has 4+ chars and is a prefix of the other. Path stems for a deliverable path: split on non-alphanumerics, ignore crates, src, core, tests, test, lib, mod, bin and the extensions rs, md, toml, json, txt, yml, yaml, lock, then apply the same FUNCTION_WORDS, COMMON_WORDS and PART_FILLER drop and the stemming. `test` stays a stem of part and criterion text and is ignored only in paths. Worked examples in `part_stems_worked_examples`: 'Add the --json flag to status' = {json, flag, statu}; 'Document the flag in the guide' = {docume, flag, guide}; 'Cover the flag with a timeout test' = {cover, flag, timeou, test}; 'Add a core test for the timeout' = {test, timeou}; '[content] docs/guide.md describes --json' = {docume, descri, json} (the path token is dropped; the path adds {docume, guide} only when it is a deliverable the criterion contains); 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' = {test, fail, change}; criterion '[behavior] Run cargo test -p athena-core --test timeout' = {} ; path stems of crates/athena-core/tests/foo.rs = {foo}.
decisions.reason: Finding 2: a stock `cargo test -p athena-core` criterion had stems {core, test} and covered a dropped 'core test' part; now it has none. Finding 6: 'athena' is a COMMON_WORDS entry, so no stem can be 'athena'. The pooled path stems (decision 6) are the only path contribution. The alias keeps 'docs/guide.md describes --json' covering '(2) Document the flag in the guide'.

rejected.option: Apply PATH_WORDS only to deliverable paths
rejected.why: Finding 2: criterion text keeps core and test from commands and paths.

rejected.option: Drop `test` from all stems
rejected.why: 'a test fails when the timeout is missing' must still cover a test part.

rejected.option: Drop the alias and require 4-letter stems
rejected.why: 'docs/guide.md describes --json' would be falsely refused.

decisions.choice: 6. Coverage. For each kind with 2+ parts, drop from every part the stems that occur in every part of that kind (fallback to the full set if that empties a part); n is the remaining count; need = min(2,n) for Enumerated, min(1,n) for Bullet; n = 0 is skipped. A part is covered when (a) one usable criterion, pooled with the path stems of every deliverable path whose text the criterion contains, shares at least `need` stems with it, or (c) a usable criterion cites the marker of an Enumerated part (`(N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c`; not bare `N)`) and shares at least 1 distinctive stem. A deliverable path alone never covers. `out_of_scope` never covers. The error says 'cover it with a deliverable and a criterion'.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3: a path alone does not cover a part. Dropping shared stems stops a criterion for part (2) covering part (3) through the shared subject 'flag'. The tension is named in the doc comment: stricter refuses more reworded readings, looser misses dropped parts. Athena's replay holds a candidate whose newly refused share exceeds the declared 10% plus 5 points, 15% (replay.rs:296-308).

rejected.option: Keep rule (b), a deliverable path alone covers, with generic path words removed
rejected.why: Still lets a path cover a part with no criterion.

rejected.option: Assign each criterion to its one best part
rejected.why: More logic and tie rules than dropping shared stems.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text
rejected.why: The summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would look covered.

decisions.choice: 7. Criterion-side negation is scoped to a clause and to the part. DEFER_PHRASES: follow-up job, follow up job, in a follow-up, in a follow up, as a follow-up, as a follow up, separate job, next job, later job, not in this job, deferred to, can wait. CRITERION_NEGATION = DEFER_PHRASES plus out of scope, out-of-scope, deferred, postponed, not done, not covered, left out, not part of. CRITERION_MARKER_NEGATION = CRITERION_NEGATION plus skipped, omitted, excluded, bare later, defer, skip, follow-up, follow up, followup, for now. `negation_hit(criterion, part)` splits the criterion into clauses at '. ', '; ', ', ', ': ' and ' and ', ' but ', ' while ', ' so '. A clause is relevant when it holds a word whose stem matches a distinctive stem of the part, or (marker list, Enumerated parts only) cites the part's marker. A CRITERION_NEGATION phrase in a relevant clause, or a marker-list phrase in a marker-citing clause, makes the criterion unusable for that part, unless the part's own text holds the phrase. A criterion unusable for one part may cover another. The error lists each ignored criterion with its phrase.
decisions.reason: Criteria here often describe refusal behaviour ('moves it to out_of_scope as a follow-up'); the phrase cancels only next to the part's own subject. 'The timeout test is deferred' still cannot cover part (3); 'status lists skipped checks' still covers '(2) Report skipped checks in status'. Bullets have no marker, so for them only CRITERION_NEGATION in a relevant clause applies. Finding 4's removal of skip/skipped/omitted/excluded concerns the request side only (decision 8).

rejected.option: Count a phrase anywhere in the criterion
rejected.why: Cancels criteria that mention refusal in another clause.

rejected.option: A flat list where skipped, omitted and excluded cancel every criterion
rejected.why: Refuses 'status lists skipped checks'.

decisions.choice: 8. Request-side deferral (finding 4). A part is skipped as deferred when (i) its own text holds a DEFER_PHRASES phrase ('(3) Add a dashboard in a follow-up job'), or (ii) another sentence of `request_own_lines`, taken outside every part span (spans blanked before splitting at '. ', '! ', '? ' and newlines), cites its marker as `(N)`, `N)`, `part N`, `item N`, `(c)`, `part c` or `item c` and holds a REQUEST_DEFERRAL phrase in some clause. REQUEST_DEFERRAL is only criterion 4's words with close variants: 'out of scope', 'out-of-scope', 'for now', 'defer', 'deferred', 'follow-up', 'follow up', 'followup', and 'later' in the restricted forms 'later' as the last word of its clause, 'at a later', 'for later', 'for a later', 'come later'. Skip, skipped, omitted and excluded are NOT request-side words. Clauses are split at '; ', ', ', ': ', ' but ', ' while '. The negator guard (not, n't, never, cannot, after removing 'not in this job', 'not part of', 'not done', 'not covered') applies only to the clause that holds the deferral phrase. So 'Part (3) is out of scope for now; do not touch athena.toml.' defers (3), 'Part (3) must not be deferred.' does not, 'In (2), skip blank lines.' and 'For (1), excluded files are listed.' do not, and 'In (2), later entries override earlier ones.' does not (bare 'later' mid-clause). The same sentence scan runs over the retried request and the retry text of decision 2. Parts of a text with no marker citation outside the parts are never deferred by (ii). '(2) Reject future timestamps', '(1) List each file separately', '(3) Defer the flush until exit' and '(3) Add a latest-value column' stay required. Stated departure from criterion 4: bare 'later' inside a part's own text ('(3) Add the dashboard later') does not defer it. 'Parts 2 and 3 can come later' cites only part 2 (word-boundary 'part N'); a stated limit.
decisions.reason: The marker citation is the guard against stray words, and the clause-scoped negator guard keeps a clarifying second clause from flipping the result. Matching criterion 4's words keeps 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' and 'Part 3 can come later.' working.

rejected.option: Whole-sentence negator guard
rejected.why: Finding 4: a later 'do not touch athena.toml' clause would leave an explicitly deferred part required.

rejected.option: Broad MARKER_NEGATION list on the request side (skip, skipped, omitted, excluded)
rejected.why: Finding 4: 'In (2), skip blank lines.' would defer a part the request wants done.

rejected.option: Narrow DEFER_PHRASES only for request sentences
rejected.why: 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' would leave the part required and the reader could not follow the request.

rejected.option: Broad list for the part's own text
rejected.why: Exempts real parts such as '(3) Defer the flush until exit'.

decisions.choice: 9. Enforce by code only. The doc comment and CHANGELOG say why information alone is not enough: the reader already sees the request and still deferred part (3) in jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k, so a refusal rule is the allowed fix. 'Pass the parsed request parts to the reader' is named as a follow-up, not done. No prompt is edited (reader budget 1998 of 2000, docs/system-facts.md). The refusal text reaches the reader on its one corrected re-read (reading.rs:738-759).
decisions.reason: No token headroom in the reader prompt, and a prompt line is not a mechanism.

rejected.option: Add a rule line to the reader prompt
rejected.why: No budget; prose only.

rejected.option: Build the parsed parts into the reader brief now
rejected.why: A larger change across briefs and budgets.

decisions.choice: 10. Measure with the producer-loop replay and act on its send-back (finding 5). After the parts code compiles, the producer's loop runs `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294-2319) once the change list touches `crates/` (`touches_reading_rules`, replay.rs:314). It replays the newest accepted readings through the candidate and sends the list of newly refused readings and the share back, against the limit `replay_limit_percent(declared)` = declared 10 + 5 (replay.rs:304-308). For each listed reading the producer decides whether a part was really dropped or the refusal is false (a reworded part, a deferral wording, a retried request). It fixes a false refusal in the matcher (stems, groups, deferral words) and adds a corpus case for its shape. It reports the measured share and the count by kind in its report. It never raises the declared 10% or the margin to fit the result, and never edits a stored reading. A refusal that is real counts toward the share as intended. If no replay runs ('no replay: <reason>' because records are absent), the report says so and states that 10% is an estimate.
decisions.reason: The 10% is an unmeasured estimate (records/ is absent from the snapshot), and a share above the limit fails the job late at the verification hold. The loop replay is the one place the producer sees the list.

rejected.option: Rely on the hold at verification alone
rejected.why: The producer would never see the list and an above-limit share would fail the job after the work is done.

rejected.option: Raise the declared share to fit the measured result
rejected.why: It hides a matcher gap; a declaration is made before the measure.

risks.risk: False refusals of good readings that reword a part so it shares too few distinctive stems with any criterion; stricter matching refuses more, looser misses dropped parts. Cleaning criterion text removes stems a criterion used to contribute (paths, commands).
risks.mitigation: Tension named in the doc comment. Bullets need one distinctive stem; n = 0 parts are skipped; filler and gate words are filtered; a marker-citing criterion with one distinctive stem covers an Enumerated part; one criterion pools with the paths it names; the error names the part, the repair and each ignored criterion, and the reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The proxy test and the own-reading case guard the common case. The 10% is an estimate; the loop replay (plan step 12) measures it.

risks.risk: A retry whose original request had parts that the earlier job already landed, or that the retry text narrows in words outside the deferral list, is refused on parts the person no longer wants.
risks.mitigation: Only the retried job's request is added, never followed-up or cited jobs. The retry text's sentences count for deferral ('Part 3 can come later'). The error names the part and the repair (a criterion). Stated as a limit in the doc comment, CHANGELOG and this list; the corpus pins the covered, deferred and dropped retry cases.

risks.risk: A request sentence that cites a marker with a deferral word is read as a deferral when it is not ('In (2), later entries ...', 'Parts 2 and 3 can come later' naming only part 2).
risks.mitigation: Marker citation is required; 'later' counts only in restricted forms; the negator guard is per clause; skip, skipped, omitted and excluded are not request-side words. The Refuse cases `request-parts-request-says-part-must-not-be-deferred`, `-skip-word-in-other-part-does-not-defer`, `-excluded-word-does-not-defer` and `-later-entries-does-not-defer` pin it; 'Parts N and M' lists are a stated limit. A missed deferral is refused with text telling the reader to cover the part.

risks.risk: Bare 'later' in a part's own text is not a deferral, so a reading that follows '(3) Add the dashboard later' is refused (stated departure from criterion 4's wording, which speaks of a sentence outside the part).
risks.mitigation: Stated in the doc comment and pinned by `request-parts-part-own-text-later-stays-required`; the request can defer with a sentence naming the marker.

risks.risk: Alternatives grouping misses a form (an 'or' inside one part, 'either' with no markers) so one option is required, or an introducer is read where none was meant.
risks.mitigation: Groups need a phrase that introduces alternatives or an ' or ' before the last marker; bare 'pick', 'choose' and 'one of' group nothing; limits are in the doc comment; corpus cases cover each form, each lead-in that must not group, and a none-covered Refuse.

risks.risk: The shared filter changes `plain_request_prose` output by accident, moving defined-terms results.
risks.mitigation: The helper holds the same loop; `plain_request_prose_is_unchanged_by_the_shared_filter`, the defined-terms corpus cases and `approve_request_has_the_generators_shapes` run in `cargo test --locked`.

risks.risk: The added `let request = ...` line in `refusing_check` breaks a source-order test that scans the body, or the shadow leaks into an earlier step.
risks.mitigation: The line sits directly before the last step, after every other step, so no other check reads it. The producer runs `cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests` and the corpus self-checks; a scan that miscounts is fixed by moving the line, never by weakening the scan.

risks.risk: An existing scripted or stored reading whose request has an Acceptance heading or enumerated markers is newly refused, forcing edits outside the listed files (reading.rs:7396, 7743; steward.rs tests; run/tests.rs; drain.rs).
risks.mitigation: Dash bullets count only inside an Acceptance section. The producer runs the listed package tests, repairs the fixture's criteria never the check, and names the file in the report.

risks.risk: A part-like list after the Acceptance section ends, an Acceptance heading written another way, or a part inside a fence is not enforced.
risks.mitigation: A stated narrow rule with the exact four headings in the doc comment; copied text and fences must not become parts.

risks.mitigation: Stem sets are pinned by `part_stems_worked_examples`; the fixture keeps 'flag' in all three parts on purpose; a count that differs from the plan is reported with the stem set shown. Corpus Accept case `request-parts-approved-work-copied-sections-ignored`, built on `generated_approval_request` (refusal_corpus.rs:1362), whose copied text after '## Source' holds 'Acceptance:' dash bullets, a numbered list, an inline '(1) .. (2) ..' line and a fenced 'Request:' block. Related Accept cases: `request-parts-fenced-acceptance-ignored`, `request-parts-quoted-proposal-enumeration-ignored`, `request-parts-cause-title-enumeration-ignored`; Refuse `request-parts-handwritten-cause-line-is-a-part`. Unit test `request_parts_skip_copied_and_generated_text` asserts none of those lines yields a part. The existing tests `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` and `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` (anchor at refusal_corpus.rs:2927) pass because every `step!` has a refusing case and the new step is last.

demonstrations.method: A new unit test module in crates/athena-core/src/reading/replay.rs, `steward_request_bullets_become_bullet_parts_only`, builds requests with `StewardRequest::new(..).render()` (steward.rs:535, 639) and asserts `request_parts` returns only Bullet parts, as many as the acceptance bullets and none from the `Files:` line. In refusal_corpus.rs `generated_requests_with_typical_readings_are_accepted` runs `refusing_check` over every generated-request shape (root_cause_request 280-297, `generated_root_cause_request`, the cause-title shape, the StewardRequest-style request with a `Files:` line, an approved-work request) with `base_reading` plus a variant with bullets reworded to keep one distinctive word, and asserts none is refused by `check_request_parts`. A retry shape (attempt request with parts, reading covering all of them) is in the same proxy. The case `request-parts-this-jobs-own-reading-accepted` rebuilds this job's retry request ('try again on 20261030-060839-1njk', with the retried request as `attempt`) and its accepted reading, whose criteria say 'as a follow-up' and 'deferred' while describing refusal tests, and is Accept. `request_parts_refusal_is_declared_intended` (modelled on `design_existing_code_refusal_is_declared_intended`, refusal_corpus.rs:2945-2993) asserts `replay_declaration` on 'expected 10% of newly refused readings' gives `share == Some(10)`, and that the doc comment and CHANGELOG hold 'higher refusal rate is intended'. The real measure is the producer-loop replay (decision 10, plan step 12): the producer reads its send-back, classifies each newly refused past reading, fixes false refusals in the matcher and reports the measured share; the 10% is an estimate, not measured.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus generated_requests_with_typical_readings_are_accepted && cargo test -p athena-core reading::replay && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus request_parts_refusal_is_declared_intended
demonstrations.observes: Zero new false refusals on the generated shapes including the standard Steward bullets and the retry shape; the declaration parses as 10; the own-reading case is accepted. The change refuses more readings and the higher rate is intended; expected 10% of newly refused readings, an estimate to be replaced by the loop replay's measured share in the report.
demonstrations.fails_without: A false refusal of a generated shape or a Steward bullet fails the proxy test; without the doc sentence or CHANGELOG text the declaration test fails.

The replay.rs test module and the proxy tests are added by plan steps 7 and 10. Local proxy only; `loop_replay` (run/mod.rs:2294) and the hold read `records/`, absent from the snapshot.

demonstrations.method: Corpus case `request-parts-inline-part-three-deferred-sza7` (Refuse by `check_request_parts`) and `request-parts-inline-all-three-kept-bw7k` (Accept); both name jobs 20261029-084645-sza7 and 20261029-110953-bw7k in `source` and say the shape is rebuilt from the introspection's account (the recorded request text is not in the snapshot). The three parts share the subject 'check timeouts'. The sza7 reading puts part 3 in `out_of_scope` and names crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs (the timeout file, not reading/checks.rs), crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/status_durations.rs, crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs, crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs and crates/athena-core/src/status.rs as already landed or rejected. The bw7k reading keeps all three parts in criteria. `sza7_and_bw7k_shapes_are_in_the_corpus` asserts both ids with the two jobs in `source` and the checks.rs path in the sza7 out_of_scope. A retry variant, `request-parts-retry-of-sza7-drops-part-three` (attempt request holds the three parts, current text 'try again on 20261029-084645-sza7', reading defers part 3), is Refuse.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus sza7_and_bw7k_shapes_are_in_the_corpus && git diff --stat

demonstrations.method: Run Athena's three checks on the final tree as separate commands. Before finishing the producer also runs `cargo test -p athena-core run::`, `cargo test -p athena-core steward::tests`, `cargo test -p athena-core work_decisions`, `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and `cargo test -p athena-cli`, and repairs any pre-existing fixture whose scripted or stored reading is newly refused (its criteria, never the check or the thresholds), naming the file in the report.
